### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **10** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/mcp`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/service-storage`, touching **88** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **5** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/security/index.ts`, `packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.batch-equivalence.golden.json`, `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/comment-access-hooks.ts`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**64** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ac8fede8f938439d2228f5b1404042d113a3812e`.

⛔ **14** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **5** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/security/index.ts`, `packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.batch-equivalence.golden.json`, `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/comment-access-hooks.ts`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `sys_user (symbol, 50 pages)`, `sys_user (literal, 50 pages)`
- **10** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **95** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ac8fede8f938439d2228f5b1404042d113a3812e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c34259fe23d799a221db4be1d56b6557083ec9b0` — the merge of head `1a141938af8791a9c67908a55a8f23e2636d2e76` into base `ac8fede8f938439d2228f5b1404042d113a3812e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c34259fe23d799a221db4be1d56b6557083ec9b0 && git checkout c34259fe23d799a221db4be1d56b6557083ec9b0
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ac8fede8f938439d2228f5b1404042d113a3812e 1a141938af8791a9c67908a55a8f23e2636d2e76 && git checkout -B drift-repro ac8fede8f938439d2228f5b1404042d113a3812e && git merge --no-ff 1a141938af8791a9c67908a55a8f23e2636d2e76

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ac8fede8f938439d2228f5b1404042d113a3812e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs ac8fede8f938439d2228f5b1404042d113a3812e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### ① Derived judgments

Each accept-set or public-surface change the diff implies, named right or wrong against ADR-0151 D3 on `main`:

1. **The resolver's `sys_user` read is unconditional** (`resolve-authz-context.ts`, `getUserRow()` joins wave 1 for every caller). Right. The only path that skipped it was a caller seeding both an email and `ai_seat`; key scopes are refused in `keys.ts`, so no live caller seeds `ai_seat` and no live path gains a read. The read is memoised (`userRowLoaded`), so the config-anchor and `ai_access` reads below reuse it: one read by primary key per resolution, as the forced pins now assert (platform-admin-config: 1 on both postures; cache pin 5: 2 for two real resolutions, 0 on a hit). Fault handling: `tryFind` throws `AuthzStoreUnavailableError` for any failed read that is not a missing table (commit 6a180e42d), so a store fault on the kind read fails LOUD and closed, never as a person; a missing `sys_user` table (`[]`) reads as a person, which is the pre-column store and correct. The ADR's O3 paragraph had the kind carried on key admission's `USER_BAN_FIELDS` read instead; the tree reads it in the resolver, which every key face (REST `computeExecCtx`, `/mcp`, stdio) passes through, so the admitted set is identical and the dev's reason (a projected read naming a column an unmigrated store lacks could refuse every key) holds — nit F3, no contract effect.
2. **An `agent` row resolves as `principalKind: 'agent'`**, is withheld the `everyone` anchor (`!agentAccount && !holdsExternalIdentity(...)`), carries `systemPermissions: []`, gains no platform standing from an anchor grant (`anchorsPlatformStanding(grant) && active && !agentAccount`) nor from the configured-administrator address (`!agentAccount && ...`), and `isTenantAdmin` is false whatever `ORGANIZATION_ADMIN_GRANTS` it holds, so `posture` is `MEMBER`. Right against D3 (explicit grants only; never an administrator). `hasPlatformAdminStanding` is `posture === 'PLATFORM_ADMIN'` over the same resolution, so the id-shaped predicate answers false for an account too (pinned). `isAgentAccountRow` reads `principal_kind` then `principalKind`, the exact literal `'agent'` only; every other value and an absent row is a person — right, and matches plugin-auth's sign-in refusals.
3. **The shared assembler**: `account = !anonymous && authz.principalKind === 'agent'` takes precedence over the OAuth arm; the account gets `principalKind: 'agent'`, `systemPermissions: []`, its own `permissions`, no `onBehalfOf`, no `performedBy`, no `oauthScopes`. Right. The precedence is safe because D2 (PR-1, merged) refuses every session for an agent row, so no OAuth consent and no token can name an account; the OAuth-delegated CONTROL keeps today's shape byte for byte (pinned in `assemble-execution-context.test.ts` and the runtime rig).
4. **The clamp sits at the one choke point.** `resolvePermissionSetsForContextUnmemoized` applies `clampPermissionSetsToAgentCeiling` after both resolutions (the named sets and the restricted fallback) for every `principalKind === 'agent'` context. Read on the head, every evaluator reaches sets through the memoised `resolvePermissionSetsForContext`: the authz middleware (object CRUD, VAMA, write-check, pre-image floor), the read filter and RLS, field readers (FLS masks and forbidden writes), object admission, operation principals (the batch path), all four sharing-verdict hosts, authored-row write, explain access, the security service and effective access. The two direct `permissionEvaluator.resolvePermissionSets` calls outside it are `describePositionGrants` (a description of a position's declared sets, no evaluation) and `resolveFallbackPermissionSets` (the HUMAN baseline, never reached on the agent branch, which floors at the restricted set). `permissionSetMemoKey` already keys on `principalKind`, so a person and an agent naming the same sets never share a memo entry; the grants cache keys on `(userId, tenantId, seeds)` and caches the envelope with its `principalKind`. Right: no cache, batch, FLS, sharing or explain path bypasses the clamp.
5. **What the clamp clears**: `viewAllRecords`, `modifyAllRecords` and `DESTRUCTIVE_CLASS_KEYS` on every `objects` entry including `'*'`; `systemPermissions` / `system_permissions` emptied; `adminScope` / `admin_scope` removed; JSON-string columns parsed as the delegated-administration gate parses them; a clean set returned as the same object, a breaching one as a fresh copy (catalogs never mutated). `DESTRUCTIVE_CLASS_KEYS` is derived from `DESTRUCTIVE_OPERATIONS` through `OPERATION_TO_PERMISSION`, so it reads `allowTransfer`, `allowRestoreOwnDeleted`, `manageRecycleBin` and follows the map. With both bypass bits cleared a `'*'` entry stops being the superuser wildcard (ADR-0066 D2 reads the two bits; the field merge's superuser vote reads the same two). Right against D3's list: View/Modify All, the destructive class, a system permission, a superuser wildcard, an admin scope.
6. **The refusal at assignment** (`agent-account-grant-refusal.ts`): `beforeInsert`/`beforeUpdate` at priority 45 on `sys_user_permission_set` and `sys_user_position`, after the ceiling-set (35) and membership (40) refusals; judges the row image AFTER the write (payload else `previous`); stands down on `isSystem`, on no `sys_user` object in the composition, on a holder the caller's own door does not read (`callerReadsGrantHolder === false`), and on a catalog read fault (warn, proceed); refuses `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` / `invalid_value` at `permission_set` or `position` naming the set and each breaching bit. Right: the loud early answer D3 asks for, the clamp the guarantee. A person's grant is never judged (the `isAgentAccount` read gates it), so no existing write narrows. Pinned on a real ObjectQL + SQLite engine with the real SecurityPlugin, including the update that moves a person's breaching grant onto the account. One nit (F2 below).
7. **`callerReadsGrantHolder`** (new export of `grant-holder-membership-refusal.ts`): the membership refusal's per-write memoised caller read, now returning the tri-state (`undefined` when the dispatch carries no caller api) and `holderLeftToReferenceCheck` re-derived as `reads === false`. Right; the membership refusal's own behaviour is unchanged (its pins run in the plugin-security suite).
8. **Inventory**: `dispatchFlowAction` and `buildAutomationContext` forward `principalKind: 'agent'` only for an agent WITHOUT `onBehalfOf`; `seedRunGrants` seeds it from the resolver beside the grants and deletes it with them (`needsGrants`), and the decider switch drops it with the trigger user's other facts; `resolveRunDataContext` carries it onto every CRUD node; the action audit line names the account as acting for itself; `connectorConnectionDelegatedCaller` returns the new `agent_account` member before `oauth`/`api_key` (still refused by that door, as every non-person caller is); the comment, attachment and mention gates and `buildContextForUser` stamp the kind; `describeEffectiveAccess` lists the restricted set as the account's `default`. Right. Read beyond the inventory: `apiForwardAgentOf` returns `undefined` for an account (no `oauthScopes`), so an `api` action forward carries the account's own key — D3 rule 5 as written; the `/mcp` door treats an undefined `oauthScopes` as "not scope-limited", so the account's tools are bounded by its grants alone — D3's MCP paragraph as written. No remaining reader of `principalKind === 'agent'` in the tree assumes `onBehalfOf` or `oauthScopes` (grep over `packages/`, non-test).
9. **Standing guards**: `ADMIN_STANDING_SURFACE.sys_user.columns` gains `principal_kind` and `principalKind` with a reason, and `STANDING_KEY_EXCLUSIONS.sys_user` carries both with the immutability reason. Right; the exactness pin (`admin-standing-surface.test.ts`, "declares exactly the columns read") is in Test Core, pending.
10. **Public surface**: core root gains `isAgentAccountRow` (widening). `ResolvedAuthzContext.principalKind`, `UserAuthzGrants.principalKind`, `FlowUserGrants.principalKind`, `RunIdentityContext.principalKind`, `SeededRunContext.principalKind` are new optional fields (widening). `DESTRUCTIVE_CLASS_KEYS`, the clamp functions, `registerAgentAccountGrantRefusal`, `callerReadsGrantHolder` and `runPrincipalKind` are module exports, not package-root exports (plugin-security's root exports only `PermissionEvaluator` from that module; service-automation's root export list from `runtime-identity.js` does not name `runPrincipalKind`); `ConnectorConnectionDelegatedCaller` is not re-exported from the runtime root. Nothing is removed or retyped. The PR body's "one export is added to plugin-security" overstates a module export as a package export — nit F4.
11. **WRONG at one consumer (should-fix F1)**: the account's envelope keeps the NAMES of the sets it holds on `permissions` (the test fixtures assert `admin_full_access` stays named; the clamp acts on bodies), and `packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts#isOverrideActor` derives standing from those names — `perms.includes(ADMIN_FULL_ACCESS)` is the platform arm (it crosses the tenant wall) and `holdsTenantAdminRung(perms)` (`ORGANIZATION_ADMIN_GRANTS.some(...)`) the tenant arm, each deliberately kept beside the `posture` read "so a transport that never resolved posture still reads the held capability"; `holdsTenantAdminRung` also builds the `admin_rescue` administrators' slate over each candidate's `resolveUserAuthzGrants`. So an account whose grant row names `admin_full_access` or `organization_admin*` is an approvals override actor (approve, reject, reassign, recall any PENDING request; across every organization for `admin_full_access`) and a rescue-slate administrator — standing the changeset says it never has, "whatever it holds". Every one of those three sets breaches by body (`ADMIN_FULL_ACCESS_CAPABILITIES` carries the `'*'` bypass bits and system permissions; `organization_admin` carries them; `organization_admin_no_bypass` carries `organization_admin`'s system permissions verbatim), so a NON-system assignment is refused by name; the row is reachable through a system or seed writer (row 23g admits it), through the refusal's own stand-downs (no hook registry, catalog read fault, unreadable holder), and no account row can exist before PR-3. The clamp cannot close it, because a name is not a bit it clears. Grade: should-fix. Fix: withhold the admin-standing names (`ADMIN_FULL_ACCESS`, `ORGANIZATION_ADMIN_GRANTS`) from an account's `permissions` in `resolveUserAuthzGrants` — the changeset's own remedy says an administrative grant "is a person's to hold" — or make the two approvals arms read `posture` alone when `context.principalKind === 'agent'`; either way pin it (an account holding `admin_full_access` is not an override actor and not on the rescue slate), and correct the changeset sentence if the name-withholding is not chosen.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/31739-ai-service-account-ceiling.md`: `patch` on all ten packages the diff moves (`core`, `mcp`, `objectql`, `plugin-audit`, `plugin-auth`, `plugin-security`, `rest`, `runtime`, `service-automation`, `service-storage`; `platform-objects` is not touched, correctly absent). Both declarations line-initial in the PR body and the changeset body: `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`. The level follows the kind alone: `none` takes `patch`; the `(narrowing)` arm is BREAKING, so the `!` headline, the BREAKING banner and the ADR-0087 disposition `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` are present and correct (no key, export or shape removed or retyped; nothing stored to migrate; no tombstone). The banner carries the before/now/remedy and the measured first-party count (0 of 3). Check Changeset is green on the head. Right. Nit: the changeset's "is never a platform or organization administrator, whatever it holds" is the sentence F1 makes untrue at one consumer until the fix lands; the fix either makes it true or rewords it.

Clause-②: no (narrowing) — confirmed on the tree: no published key, export or shape is removed or retyped; the only published accept-set change is a narrowing of what an agent principal's sets grant at evaluation and one refused class of non-system assignment write.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev flag (1) — the assignment refusal's unreadable-holder stand-down and `callerReadsGrantHolder`.** Answered. The first cut read an unreadable holder as the system (8 reds in the membership and tenant-wall suites); the head reuses the membership refusal's per-write memoised caller read and stands down when it answers `false`, so the refusal never names the kind of a user the caller cannot read; the clamp still holds for such a row. Consistent with the membership refusal's discipline and with ADR-0090 D6's indistinguishability. Nit F2: the account refusal does not consult `referenceCheckAsksCaller` first (the membership refusal does), so it stands down on an unreadable holder even where the engine's reference check reads as the system and will not refuse the row either; the grant is then stored unjudged and clamped at evaluation. Row 23g states the stand-down. No correctness effect.
- **Dev flag (2) — off-surface edits.** `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx` row 23g plus the regenerated register are what `check:system-context-census` demands for a new `isSystem` stand-down (both hooks named with their rows); the Lint gates on the head are green. `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` gains one row written by that gate's own `--write` for the runtime rig's driven `findOne` double. Both accepted as the gates' own output, not reviewed.
- **Dev flag (3) — skills/docs follow-up owed** (`content/docs/ai/agents.mdx`, `content/docs/permissions/index.mdx`). Acceptable to defer: an author first meets an account at PR-3's registration door, and documenting a door that does not exist advertises a capability the runtime does not yet deliver (Prime Directive #10). Condition: PR-3 carries the teaching in the same PR as the door; the card keeps the debt visible. No escalation.
- **Dev flag (4a) — a `runAs:'system'` flow triggered by an account.** Out of the declared narrowing: ADR-0151 Non-goals list "a flow or job `runAs` naming an account (ADR-0073's automation principal stays the identity of user-less runs)" as not decided, and D3's "never runs `isSystem`" reads on the principal, not on a flow the author declared system. A `runAs:'system'` run is the flow author's grant and is the same system run for any member who may trigger it; the account is the trigger, not the acting identity, and the trigger door now carries its kind. Refusing it at the trigger door would narrow every automation an account may trigger, which is a narrowing beyond this PR's declaration and ADR-0151's scope: it goes to the maintainer (an ADR-0151 amendment or an O6 decision), not into PR-3. B is safe: it adds no power the account did not have the moment a flow author chose `runAs:'system'`, and O2/O6 are the ADR's named readers of `principalKind`. Recommend B with a follow-up card that names the question.
- **Dev flag (4b) — sets bound through identity positions (`org_owner`, `org_admin`) clamped but not withheld.** Within the declared narrowing's mechanism: the clamp is what the PR declares, and the positions reach `positions` as a projection the approvals and security plugin deliberately no longer read as authority. Withholding them would be a further narrowing on accounts only; nothing writes one today (PR-1's reconciler binds no identity position to an account; a non-system `sys_user_position` write naming a position whose sets breach is refused by this PR's position arm), so B is safe for this PR. PR-3 may revisit with its own declaration, since registration is where an account's membership row is born; it is not a maintainer question. Note the same name-based reader as F1 applies to `permissions` names, not to position names.

### ④ Design judgment

**The narrowing against the published spec.** ADR-0151 D3 on `main` (merged `cae8d8fe`) already states every refusal this PR makes real: explicit grants only (no `everyone` anchor, no member baseline, the restricted floor); rule 2's ceiling held at evaluation (View/Modify All, the destructive class, a system permission, a superuser wildcard, an admin scope); refusal by name at assignment; never an administrator. Nothing is taken from a consumer that the spec declared: an OAuth-delegated agent's three first-party sets (`mcp_agent_data_read` = `{'*': {allowRead}}`, `mcp_agent_data_write` = `{'*': CRUD}` plus the managed-write denies, `mcp_agent_restricted` = `{}`) carry none of the cleared bits, read in `default-permission-sets.ts` on the head, so the measured census (0 of 3 clamped) is credible from the tree and is pinned over the live `defaultPermissionSets` list with identity (`toBe`) on each. A deployment that edited its own `mcp_agent_*` set to carry a bypass bit sees a narrower answer, which is exactly what the changeset's BREAKING banner says.

**Human principals and the OAuth CONTROL.** Every behavioural branch is gated on `agentAccount` (resolver) or `principalKind === 'agent'` (plugin-security, assembler account arm, automation doors). A person holding the same rows as the account resolves with the `everyone` anchor, the system permission and platform standing (CONTROLs in core, rest, mcp, runtime, plugin-security). The OAuth-delegated agent keeps `onBehalfOf`, `performedBy`, scope-derived `permissions` and the delegator's `systemPermissions` under `delegatesActions`; its side of the intersection is clamped by the same line, a no-op on the first-party sets; the delegator's side (`principalKind: 'human'`) is untouched. Correct.

**Bypass hunt.** Cache: the grants cache (`resolve-user-grants-cache.ts`) keys on identity and seeds and stores the envelope with `principalKind`; the set memo keys on `principalKind`. Batch: `resolveOperationPrincipals` is a host of the memoised resolver. FLS, sharing (all four verdict hosts), explain, effective access: hosts. Impersonation: a session for an agent row is refused by PR-1's `sessionBefore`. The OAuth ceiling path: the assembler's account arm precedes it and no token can name an account. Automation: the kind is seeded, forwarded, carried to every CRUD node and dropped at the decider switch; a body-supplied `principalKind` stays a flow param (pinned). Found one: the name-based standing read in plugin-approvals (F1, should-fix) — a standing consumer outside the ceiling's choke point that the clamp cannot reach because it reads set names, kept on the account's envelope by design. Grade stands at should-fix, not must-fix: the declared narrowing (clamp and refusal) is implemented at the one choke point every evaluation passes; the leak needs a system or seed writer to store an administrative set's name against an account, no account can exist before PR-3, and the fix is one guarded line in the resolver or the approvals gate plus a pin.

**The unconditional `sys_user` read.** Fail-closed (`AuthzStoreUnavailableError` on any read fault but a missing table), one primary-key read already memoised for the config anchor and `ai_access`, added only on the fully-seeded path no live caller takes, recorded as the sixth golden move with the pin's header saying why. Safe. The ADR's O3 paragraph placed the kind on `USER_BAN_FIELDS`; the resolver placement is a sound deviation (nit F3) and reaches every face, including a stdio process and an automation run that key admission never sees.

**The refusal.** Priority ordering, the post-write image on update, the `previous` binding, the holder-moved case and the system stand-down are right and pinned on a real engine. The catalog-fault branch proceeds with a `warn` rather than refusing; acceptable because the clamp is the guarantee and the sibling refusals do the same. `isAgentAccount` compares a placeholder-shaped id by `$startsWith` on its first character with `limit: 2`, as the membership refusal does; a placeholder-shaped id is never a stored holder, so this has no effect (nit F4b, folded into F4).

**Findings.**
- F1 — should-fix: `plugin-approvals#isOverrideActor` and the `admin_rescue` slate read `admin_full_access` / `ORGANIZATION_ADMIN_GRANTS` by NAME off `permissions`; the account's envelope keeps those names; the clamp clears bits, not names. Withhold the names for an account in the resolver (or read `posture` alone for `principalKind === 'agent'` in both arms), pin it, and keep or reword the changeset sentence.
- F2 — nit: the account refusal stands down on an unreadable holder without first asking `referenceCheckAsksCaller`, so where the reference check reads as the system the row is stored unjudged; clamp holds; row 23g says so.
- F3 — nit: the kind is read in the resolver, not on key admission's `USER_BAN_FIELDS` read as ADR-0151's O3 paragraph sketched; equivalent admitted set, sound reason, worth one sentence in PR-3's body.
- F4 — nit: the PR body counts `DESTRUCTIVE_CLASS_KEYS` as a plugin-security package export; it is a module export (the root exports only `PermissionEvaluator` from that module). The placeholder-id branch of `isAgentAccount` mirrors the sibling and has no effect.
- F5 — nit: the access explainer attributes an account's restricted floor as a baseline (the dev's own out-of-scope note); wording only.

No must-fix. F1 earns a delta review of its fix on the next head.
